true_answer: 1.1. Additive and Multiplicative Principles 63 Example 1.1.7 Let A | { 1 , 2 } and B | { 3 , 4 , 5 } . Find A × B . Solution . We want to find ordered pairs ( a , b ) where a can be either 1 or 2 and b can be either 3, 4, or 5. A × B is the set of all of these pairs: A × B | {( 1 , 3 ) , ( 1 , 4 ) , ( 1 , 5 ) , ( 2 , 3 ) , ( 2 , 4 ) , ( 2 , 5 )} . The question is, what is | A × B | ? To figure this out, write out A × B . Let A | { a 1 , a 2 , a 3 ,..., a m } and B | { b 1 , b 2 , b 3 ,..., b n } (so | A | | m and | B | | n ).
